title: Runtime and build behavior
text: CrowPSX uses runtime material switches for PBR map layout, smoothness/roughness response, detail maps, grunge, and emission. This keeps the Surface PBR, Nature PBR, and Vertex Painting PBR feature matrices compact while preserving the same inspector controls and independent painted-layer workflows. Matching PBR shaders reuse their Default shader's ShadowCaster and lightweight Meta support passes. Unity's required Built-in Render Pipeline lighting, shadow, fog, primary-pass instancing, and lightmapping variants remain available; Forward Add omits instancing variants because Unity's Built-in forward renderer does not instance additional passes.  Disabled features avoid their major texture or lighting work. This includes grunge, AO, parallax, direct and indirect lighting, direct specular, reflection probes, emission, and optional cloud self-shading. Packed PBR reads Metallic, AO, and surface response together, while vertex-painted shaders skip texture families and parallax activation belonging to zero-weight layers. Grunge is evaluated once and shared across its surface responses. Forward Add omits unused lightmap, indirect-lighting, emission, and debug data. Light Probe Proxy Volume support follows Unity's Graphics Tier built-in define instead of adding a duplicate Forward Base permutation, and particle Forward Base passes omit unused lightmap and secondary vertex-light combinations.  Because every lit shader carries both a Universal and a Built-in SubShader, CrowPSX strips the passes belonging to the pipeline a build is not using. ForwardBase and ForwardAdd are Built-in only and go from an SRP build; the ScriptableRenderPipeline passes go from a Built-in build. Those forward passes are where the variant count lives, so this is most of the saving. ShadowCaster and Meta passes are never stripped, because both pipelines use them under the same pass type. Add the CROWPSX_DISABLE_VARIANT_STRIPPING scripting define to compile the stripper out.  Depth-volume decals use their regular pass for HDR emission in Normal, Premultiplied, and additive-family modes. The independent additive emission pass is enabled only when a Multiply decal has non-zero HDR Emission Strength. In the skybox, disabling Cloud Self Shading removes its additional cloud-density read.

title: Performance
text: Runtime switches, feature cost, pipeline stripping, and variants.

title: A material is pink or uses Unity's default inspector
text: Allow Unity to finish importing, then reselect the material. Read the first CrowPSX-related error in the Console and reimport the complete CrowPSX folder without moving or renaming its shader or Editor files.

title: Shader compilation takes a long time
text: The first import compiles Unity's required lighting, shadow, fog, instancing, and lightmapping combinations, and every lit shader carries both a Universal and a Built-in SubShader so it survives a pipeline switch. CrowPSX keeps its own PBR feature combinations compact, and builds strip the passes belonging to the pipeline you are not using, but the initial import is still the slowest step.  Allow the current import to finish before reimporting the package again. Editing any file under Shaders/Shared recompiles every shader family that includes it. If changing only a material property starts a full shader import, check whether another editor extension is forcing asset refreshes.

title: Shaders report Universal Render Pipeline include errors
text: Every lit CrowPSX shader carries both a Universal and a Built-in SubShader, and Unity compiles both at import. A generated define tells the Universal passes whether the URP package is actually present; it is normally kept in step automatically when URP is added or removed.  Run Tools > CrowPSX > Regenerate Pipeline Defines if it falls behind. If Unity instead warns that the generated file is missing, reimport the CrowPSX folder, it lives at Assets/CrowPSX/Shaders/Shared/CrowPSXPipeline.hlsl and the package has to stay at Assets/CrowPSX for it to be found.

title: Polybrush cannot paint the material
text: Assign a CrowPSX/Surface/Vertex Painting/... shader. Run Tools > CrowPSX > Polybrush > Configure Texture Painting . Reselect the object or leave and re-enter Polybrush Texture Paint mode.  Painted transitions depend on mesh vertices. If a blend looks blocky, increase mesh density; increasing texture resolution will not add more paintable detail.

title: A normal or packed PBR map looks incorrect
text: Import normal textures as Unity Normal Map assets. Packed PBR textures must use linear sampling with sRGB disabled and contain R Metallic, G Ambient Occlusion, B Height, and A Smoothness or Roughness. Make sure Surface Response Workflow matches the data stored in alpha.

title: Parallax looks stretched or moves incorrectly
text: Start with a low Parallax Height and a Height Floor of 0 . White height values are raised; black values are recessed. Enable Link PBR UVs if Height should follow the Albedo transform. Check that the mesh has valid, correctly oriented tangents. Raise Parallax Steps only when visible stepping requires it; values above 32 are expensive.  Parallax offsets texture coordinates. It cannot change the mesh silhouette or create true overhangs, and deliberately exaggerated height can still stretch at steep viewing angles.

title: Vertex-painted PBR is expensive
text: Each visible painted layer can contribute its own map samples. Prefer Packed Map , disable unused height effects, and keep Parallax Steps modest when multiple layers overlap. Use Separate Maps only where independent textures or transforms are necessary.

title: A depth-volume decal is missing or renders incorrectly
text: Depth-volume decals reconstruct the receiving surface from the camera depth texture. If Unity is not generating that texture, the decal may disappear, project incorrectly, or appear only under certain scene settings.  Ensure the rendering camera produces a depth texture. A Directional Light with shadows or a screen-space Ambient Occlusion effect often appears to “fix” the decal because those features also make Unity request camera depth, but neither is a requirement for the decal itself. The reliable solution is to enable or request the camera's Depth texture directly. Also confirm that the decal volume intersects opaque scene geometry and that its material uses a visible blend mode and opacity.

title: A depth-volume decal drifts or flickers under URP
text: The active Universal Renderer is missing the CrowPSX Depth Volume renderer feature. Without it URP either copies depth after the transparent queue, so the decal reconstructs receivers from the previous frame and is stable only while the camera is still, or copies vertex-snapped depth, so the decal clips against a surface that is not where it appears.  Select the decal material and press Add To Renderer in the inspector's diagnostics, or add it manually with Add Renderer Feature > CrowPSX Depth Volume on the Universal Renderer asset. Tools > CrowPSX > Validate Installation also reports this as a warning.  Because Scene view and a gizmo-enabled Game view get a depth prepass from URP anyway, the decal can look correct in one view and wrong in another until the feature is added.

title: Block Decals does not stop a depth-volume decal
text: Set the surface material to Block Decals and the decal material to Respect Blockers . Receiver and Test Receivers form a separate allow-list workflow and must be enabled as a pair.

title: Transparent objects sort incorrectly
text: Keep Z Write disabled for ordinary transparency, avoid intersecting transparent surfaces when possible, and change the render queue only when necessary. Use Cutout when hard edges are acceptable.

title: An outline is correct in the Scene view but wrong or missing in play mode
text: The mesh was baked with the older object-space encoding , and something is moving it. Static batching runs only in play mode and builds: it rewrites the combined mesh into world space and copies UV channels through verbatim, so an outline normal stored as a plain object-space direction stops describing the geometry it belongs to. The hull then extrudes the wrong way, usually disappearing on hard-edged props while rounded ones still look closed. GPU skinning does the same thing for the same reason.  Bake it again. Current bakes store the normal in each vertex's tangent frame, which both systems transform along with the mesh, so a re-baked mesh is correct batched or skinned. The Outline section and the Material Manager's Checks tab both flag meshes still carrying the old encoding, and the reuse check refuses stale encodings, so an unchanged source is genuinely re-baked rather than reported as reused.  Mesh Normals is unaffected either way, because the batcher does transform NORMAL .

title: An outline disappears up close under URP
text: Check Copy Depth Mode on the Universal Renderer. With Force Prepass (and with Depth Priming) URP writes the depth buffer from a prepass before drawing anything, and CrowPSX renders that prepass unsnapped by default so depth-volume decals get a crack-free receiver. The forward pass then draws the surface snapped, and the depth buffer describes geometry up to a snap cell away from what is on screen. The outline hull depth-tests against that mismatch and is rejected wherever the disagreement exceeds the outline width, which shows up as the outline breaking apart or vanishing at close range and grazing angles.  Turn on Snap Depth Prepass in Retro Geometry for materials that use outlines, or set Copy Depth Mode to After Opaques . Built-in never runs a prepass, so it does not show this.

title: Shadows are black under URP but correct in the Built-in pipeline
text:
The scene has Realtime Global Illumination enabled. Unity's Enlighten realtime GI is
supported in the Built-in Render Pipeline but was removed from the Universal Render Pipeline,
so nothing under URP can read its output.  This turns black when Realtime Environment Lighting is also on, because the environment
contribution then lives in the realtime GI data rather than in the baked lightmap. Built-in
reads it back and fills the shadows; URP has no realtime GI data at all, and the baked
lightmap never received that contribution, so shadows lose their fill entirely.  Open Window > Rendering > Lighting > Scene , turn off Realtime Global Illumination , and
bake again. The environment then goes into the baked lightmap, which both pipelines read.  Realtime GI is deprecated in Unity 2022 and removed in later versions, so turning it off is
also the forward-compatible choice.

title: Emission is visible but does not illuminate a baked lightmap
text: Confirm that the renderer contributes Global Illumination, receives GI from Lightmaps, and uses a material marked Baked Emissive . Enable Baked Global Illumination and bake the lighting again.

title: A Nature material does not move
text: Enable Wind and set Maximum Bend above zero. Make sure the selected Anchoring Source contains usable values. For Local Height, match Anchor Height and Full Motion Height to the mesh's local Y range. Use a mesh with enough vertices to bend.  Realtime shadows follow animated foliage. Baked lightmaps store the static rest pose, so use realtime or mixed direct shadows when animated foliage shadows are important.

title: VR or stereoscopic rendering looks incorrect
text: Use Built-in Forward rendering for Single Pass Instanced. Soft particles and depth-volume decals require camera depth. Grab Distortion uses true refraction in Multi-Pass and its stereo-safe heat-ripple fallback in Single Pass Instanced or Multiview.  If the retro motion is uncomfortable, apply the Comfort VR profile or lower VR Snap Strength and VR Affine Strength independently.

title: Requesting support
text: Include the CrowPSX version, Unity version, graphics API, exact shader name, and the first relevant Console error. For visual problems, include the material Inspector and affected object in the same screenshot.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Resolve import, lighting, material, decal, outline, and baking issues.

title: 1.1.0: Unity 6 Compatibility
text: Recent Unity 6 releases changed several URP and editor APIs. This update keeps CrowPSX working on every version from Unity 2022.3 LTS to Unity 6.6. Existing materials need no changes.

title: Compatibility
text: URP Forward+ on Unity 6.1 and newer. Point and spot lights render under Forward+, the default rendering path in new Unity 6 projects. These versions renamed the Forward+ shader keyword ( _FORWARD_PLUS to _CLUSTER_LIGHT_LOOP ); CrowPSX supports both, and builds only include the one your URP version uses. URP Deferred+ (Unity 6.6). Supported as a rendering path, including Vertex-mode lighting. Terrain on Unity 6.6. URP terrain materials render correctly after URP's terrain shader changes. Clean import on Unity 6.6. No "Script Updating Consent" dialog and no deprecation warnings in the Console. Input System projects. The demo scene runs in projects set to the Input System only, the default for new Unity 6 projects, with no Player Settings changes.

title: Changed
text: Vertex Hybrid under URP now matches Built-in: each light's shading, specular included, is calculated per vertex, while its falloff (and, on URP Forward, its shadow) is applied per pixel. The four most important point and spot lights get this treatment; any others are lit fully per vertex. Documentation. The Shader Reference now explains the three lighting modes, light limits, and which lights cast shadows in each pipeline. The demo scene documentation reflects the new input support.

title: 1.0.0: Initial Public Release
text: The first public release of CrowPSX for Unity's Built-in Render Pipeline and Universal Render Pipeline.

title: Render pipelines
text: Every lit shader carries both a Universal and a Built-in SubShader in the same shader asset, so materials survive a pipeline switch without being copied, reassigned, or upgraded. Automatic URP detection through a generated shader define, with Tools > CrowPSX > Regenerate Pipeline Defines as a manual fallback. Build-time stripping of the forward passes belonging to the pipeline a build is not using, disabled by the CROWPSX_DISABLE_VARIANT_STRIPPING scripting define. CrowPSX Depth Volume renderer feature for URP, with detection and one-click installation from the material inspector and the installation validator. CrowPSX Outline renderer feature for URP, with detection and one-click installation from the material inspector, since URP's object draw does not execute the additional outline pass on its own. CrowPSX Outline Support component as the per-scene alternative to that feature, requesting the same pass per camera so a shipped scene draws outlines without the project being set up. Built-in needs neither.

title: Shader suite
text: Surface Default, Lite, and PBR shaders. Four-layer Vertex Painting Default, Lite, and PBR shaders using Base, Red, Green, and Blue vertex-color layers. Nature Default, Lite, and PBR shaders with animated foliage deformation. Terrain PBR shader with Built-in additional-pass, basemap, and basemap-generation support, and URP terrain-contract support. Standard and Grab Distortion particle shaders. Depth Volume decal shader. HDR Procedural Skybox shader.

title: Surface rendering and retro controls
text: Pixel or vertex realtime lighting with direct, indirect, ambient, minimum-light, and stepped-lighting controls. Final-color grading and posterization. Screen-space vertex snapping, affine texture warping, and configurable pixel-snap templates. Opaque, Cutout, and Transparent rendering with alpha maps, bake-transparency maps, clipping, dithering, depth, culling, render queue, and GPU instancing controls. Stereo-stable geometry snapping for Multi-Pass, Single Pass Instanced, and Android Multiview VR. Visible VR / Stereo Comfort controls with Off, Comfort, Balanced, and Full profiles plus independent VR Snap and VR Affine strengths. Optional inverted-hull outlines on all six mesh-surface shaders, with screen-fixed or world-space width, distance fade, texture masking, and sampled base-color matching. Disabled materials submit no outline draw.

title: PBR materials
text: Separate Maps and Packed Map workflows for Surface PBR and Nature PBR, with an independent workflow for every painted PBR layer. Smoothness or Roughness surface-response workflows, including independent selection per painted layer. Normal, Metallic, Ambient Occlusion, Height, surface-response, detail, direct-specular, and reflection-probe controls. Packed PBR channel layout: R Metallic, G Ambient Occlusion, B Height, and A Smoothness or Roughness. Normal maps remain separate. Height-based parallax occlusion mapping with 1–64 integer steps, grazing-angle stabilization, Parallax Height up to 1 , and Height Floor controls. Signed normal strength from -4 to 4 , supporting inverted tangent-space relief. Specular Strength and Reflection Strength ranges from 0–4 . Linked core PBR UV transforms or independent transforms for individual maps. Runtime-efficient packed sampling, disabled-feature early-outs, and zero-weight sampling skips for painted layers. A themed packed-map creation card that previews channels, requests confirmation, creates a linear PNG beside the surface-color texture when possible, assigns it, and switches the relevant material or painted layer to Packed Map without removing separate-map assignments. Automatic Detail Packed PBR creation when enabled detail maps are packed on Surface or Nature PBR materials. Inspector channel guides and performance guidance for expensive painted Separate Maps configurations.

title: Grunge and emission
text: Grunge projection, masking, color, opacity, and blend controls on supported shaders. Normal grunge compositing for placing the masked grunge result over the underlying surface. Grunge influence across supported PBR responses, including signed height embossing and carving. Texture-driven emission with masks, UV controls, source shaping, animation, HDR color, and strength controls. Unclamped Unity Meta emission output for Progressive Lightmapper baking and Bakery-compatible alpha-meta support.

title: Vertex painting
text: Four independently authored Base, Red, Green, and Blue material layers. Independent Albedo, tint, UVs, PBR map workflow, surface-response workflow, linked UV state, maps, strengths, Parallax Height, and Height Floor per PBR layer. Shared integer Parallax Steps across the four painted layers. Normalized layer blending across Albedo, Normal, Metallic, Ambient Occlusion, Height, surface response, and texture alpha. Recommended Polybrush Texture Paint metadata and a setup helper under Tools > CrowPSX > Polybrush .

title: Nature and terrain
text: Anchored Nature wind with wind direction, sway, gusts, leaf flutter, plant variation, flex shaping, mask falloff, and presets. Local Height, Vertex Alpha, UV2 Y, and texture-mask anchoring sources, with channel selection and inversion for the mask texture. Matching realtime deformation in Forward and ShadowCaster passes; baked output uses the static rest pose. TerrainLayer Albedo, Normal, Metallic, Smoothness, holes, additional-layer rendering, distant basemaps, lighting, color, and pixel-snapping support.

title: Particles and decals
text: Particle flipbooks, masks, secondary textures, packed VFX maps, custom particle streams, soft-particle fading, dissolve, distortion, intersection effects, distance/camera fades, and presets. Grab Distortion framebuffer refraction in Multi-Pass with a stereo-safe heat-ripple fallback in Single Pass Instanced and Multiview. Depth-volume projection with Normal, Premultiplied, additive-family, and Multiply blending suitable for graffiti, stickers, lighting, and stylized volume effects. Independent Unlit Strength and unclamped HDR Emission Color/Strength for depth-volume decals. Stencil presets for Block Decals, Respect Blockers, Receiver, and Test Receivers.

title: Procedural skybox
text: HDR zenith, horizon, and ground gradients with exposure, color grading, and HDR-safe posterization. Multiple textured celestial bodies with independent placement, shape, tint, glow, and mask controls. Analytic moon phases with eight presets, phase cycle, terminator rotation and softness, earthshine, phase-aware glow, and full-disc star occlusion. Texture Alpha, Brightness (Luminance), and Alpha × Brightness celestial mask modes. Spherical star fields with configurable population, appearance, distribution, and height fading. One or two cloud layers with masks, self-shading, and lighting from the strongest enabled above-horizon Sun or Moon. Transparent surroundings/skyline rendering. Global orientation, automatic rotation, frame-stepped movement, and independent motion for celestial bodies, stars, clouds, and surroundings. Environment lighting controls that hold Unity's ambient source on Skybox, optionally filter or tint the generated ambient probe, and apply to the active scene automatically or on demand. Sky-specific diagnostics for invisible settings, costly combinations, mask configuration, cloud lighting, and motion.

title: Material authoring tools
text: Custom themed material inspectors with search, modified-only filtering, foldable groups, reset controls, contextual descriptions, and guarded high-cost ranges. Material diagnostics with severity grouping and actionable repair suggestions. Built-in and user-defined material presets. Material Manager for collecting, filtering, converting, copying, resetting, and batch-editing compatible materials. Batch rendering, lighting, preset, and VR Profile operations. Outline Normals baking, from the material inspector or Tools > CrowPSX , which writes position-welded smooth normals into UV4 so an inverted hull stays closed across hard edges, leaving surface shading untouched and the original mesh restorable. Installation validator and shader/material schema migration support.

title: Compatibility and package content
text: Unity 2022.3 LTS or newer. Built-in Render Pipeline support with Forward lighting, shadows, fog, lightmaps, reflection probes, Light Probe Proxy Volumes, and required Unity variants. Universal Render Pipeline support from the same shader assets, including its forward light loop, terrain contract, Single Pass Instanced and Multiview XR modes, and opaque-texture refraction. Baked Indirect, Shadowmask, and Subtractive mixed lighting on Surface, Vertex Painting, Nature, and Terrain materials in both render pipelines. Progressive Lightmapper HDR emission and transparency extraction through dedicated lightweight Meta passes. Bakery alpha-meta compatibility on supported surface shaders in both render pipelines. A self-contained playable demonstration scene with namespaced first-person sample scripts, referencing no content outside the package. Third-party notices, setup documentation, shader reference, workflow guides, and troubleshooting documentation.

title: Before you start
text: Run Tools > CrowPSX > Validate Installation after importing the package, and back up your project before a bulk material operation.
